prompt:
Design a Model Governance & Evaluation Workbench to run regulated scoring, plan governance, and feedback-driven model iteration entirely inside an offline corporate network. Primary roles include Administrator (system configuration and security), ML Engineer (dataset curation, training runs, model promotion), Evaluator (completes assigned evaluations), Reviewer (returns evaluations for revision and approves submissions), and Plan Owner (maintains build plans and BOM changes). The Vue.js web UI provides a left-to-right workflow that starts with selecting an evaluation cycle (for example, Q2 2026 running 04/01/2026–06/30/2026), reviewing assigned participants, and completing an evaluation form that shows template weights, real-time subtotal rollups, and clear flags when values are missing or exceed configured thresholds. State transitions are visible as a timeline badge with actionable prompts and deadline feedback, moving through Not Started, In Progress, Submitted, Returned for Revision, and Archived; reminders appear as in-app banners and a daily on-screen digest at 9:00 AM local time, with make-up evaluations allowed for up to 5 business days after a deadline when enabled by an Administrator. Build plan management is presented as a compare-and-approve experience: Plan Owners can create, copy, and compare versions, view per-change BOM diffs with notes and tags, generate an export file for offline sharing, and issue time-limited share links that require a local login and role permission. For model operations, ML Engineers can build samples, run training and evaluation, register models by version, and route selected versions to low-latency inference; an A/B toggle allows splitting traffic (default 90/10) with one-click rollback if key metrics degrade. End users can close the loop through embedded feedback controls such as Like, Not Interested, and Block, with near-real-time impact governed by experiment toggles and version rollback.

The backend uses FastAPI to expose decoupled REST-style APIs consumed by the Vue.js frontend over the local network, enforcing server-side validation, deterministic scoring, and consistent feature computation between training and inference. PostgreSQL persists users, roles, evaluation cycles, state transitions, templates and weights, calculation traces, plan versions and BOM diffs, model registry metadata, inference routing rules, experiments, and feedback events. Result calculation produces a traceable ledger per submission including source inputs, timestamp, template version, rule set version, and the exact handling applied: missing values default to zero or “exclude from denominator” based on a template rule, and outliers are flagged when outside configurable statistical bounds (default z-score > 3.0) without silently altering the value. Feature consistency checks block model promotion when training and inference feature definitions diverge, and inference requests must complete within a 150 ms server budget at p95 for approved models. Security is offline-first: login is local username/password with salted hashing (minimum 12 characters, lockout after 5 failed attempts for 15 minutes), API authentication uses signed session tokens with anti-replay timestamps (60-second skew), and baseline CSRF/XSS/SQL-injection protections are enforced. Sensitive fields are masked in the UI by default and encrypted at rest using database-level encryption, while audit logs are append-only for key actions such as add/drop, rule changes, grade edits, plan rollbacks, and model promotions. Backup and recovery are handled locally via nightly encrypted backups retained for 30 days, plus a one-click restore workflow restricted to Administrators and recorded in the audit trail.
